_comment: OSINT Industries v2 API (docs.osint.industries/reference/search-1). Reference DATA for scripts/osint/osint_industries.py — endpoints, request defaults, the selector types the API accepts, and the caveat every result carries. Auth is the `api-key` header (OSINT_INDUSTRIES_API_KEY). Billing: 1 credit per lookup, +3 when a premium module applies (premium=true); the credit lookup is free.

settings._comment: ua is an Android Chrome string (project decision: prefer an Android UA for web requests). timeout_seconds is the module deadline sent to the API (docs: recommended 60, min 25, max 80). socket_grace_seconds is added to it for the HTTP read. max_modules caps the module rows a compact summary returns.
settings.ua: Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 15; Pixel 9) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/140.0.0.0 Mobile Safari/537.36

endpoints._comment: base + paths. request is POST with a JSON body {type, query, timeout, premium, exact_match}. credits is GET and costs nothing.

types._comment: Selector types the v2 API accepts. `name` honours exact_match; `wallet` is a crypto address.

status_reasons._comment: HTTP status → reason shown to the analyst. 402 is the vendor's own credit limit (never a local cap).

entries.400: bad request — check the selector type and format
entries.401: OSINT Industries rejected the key (OSINT_INDUSTRIES_API_KEY missing or revoked)
entries.402: out of OSINT Industries credits — the vendor's limit, not a local cap

caveat._comment: Printed with every result. It is the attribution rail for this source: account existence is collected, never attributed.
caveat.text: A module hit means an account is registered to this selector TODAY; it does not say who registered it or when. Display names are self-declared. Masked email/phone hints are tail-character comparisons and are NOT identity evidence in either direction: a different hint may be a second number on the same account, and a matching tail can be coincidence. Never treat a hit as a link between two domains, never name the account holder as the operator from this alone, and never pivot to the current holders of a number that may have changed hands.
